what: The first host evidence for the only Office.js-reaching behaviour change in v0.6.1.
build: 0fde152, whose shipped bytes are identical to v0.6.1 — `git diff v0.6.1..HEAD -- src manifest*.xml vite.config.ts` is empty
host: PowerPoint on the web, pane stamp 0fde152, deck Presentation64
why: `src/core/elements.ts` gained `desc` on all five builders between 454303d (the last round-validated build before the release) and v0.6.1, and `scene.desc` flows `-> opts.altText -> Shape.altTextDescription` at three call sites in powerpoint.ts. That is a PowerPointApi 1.10 write. No scenario in selftest.ts touches Elements — grep it for harvey/kpiCard/elements and the count is 0 — so rounds 455-459 were green five times without ever asking. The manifest ships five ribbon deep links straight at these buttons, which is what a certification tester clicks first.
method: Clicked each element's own button by DOM id inside the pane's frame (all five share the accessible name "Insert", so a name lookup cannot tell them apart), then read the selected slide back through Office.js with `items/altTextDescription` NAMED in the load.

confirmed.flow: Process flow: Scope, Design, Build, Launch. Design highlighted.

unverified.table: NOT a defect, and not confirmed either. The button was enabled, the click was accepted, and the insert was attempted at 23 shapes. The host then went silent and the pane reported it: 'Failed: PowerPoint did not respond while drawing shapes 1-10 of 23 (45s) | at=drawing the chart's shapes'. The slide's shape count was 52 before and after. Same 45s silent-host stall that blind-skipped `insert onto a slide that already has content` in round 458.

conclusion: Four of the five Elements write a correct, element-specific altTextDescription on a real host. The 1.10 write reaches PowerPoint and the accessibility description a user gets is the one the engine built. The fifth is untested because the host would not draw it, which is an environment result rather than a product one — and the pane said so rather than failing silently.

secondSitting.why: To finish the table element, and to re-run the probe after it was fixed to tell `could not ask` from `asked and the answer was wrong`.
secondSitting.reconfirmed: A hand read of the settled slide returned the same four descriptions, each on a shape named PowerChart: 'Harvey ball, 75% filled.', 'Checkbox, yes.', 'Process flow: Scope, Design, Build, Launch. Design highlighted.', 'Revenue: €4.2m +12% vs LY (up).'. The host reported PowerPointApi 1.8/1.9/1.10 = true, 1.11 = false, so the 1.10 gate was open throughout.
secondSitting.table: STILL NOT CONFIRMED, and the reason is the SAME 45s stall as the first sitting — not a second, different one. RETRACTED 2026-09-17, same day, by a review that counted the parts: this entry said 'its parts arrived — rule-top, rule-header, cell-text-0-0..0-4, cell-text-1-0..1-2 — and NEVER GROUPED', and called grouping the new blocker. That is ten shapes, `SHAPES_PER_SYNC` is 10 (`powerpoint.ts:9755`), and they are the first ten of the scene in order. `buildTableScene` (`elements.ts:525`) pushes a `cell-text-<r>-<c>` for every column of every row unconditionally and a `rule-bottom` unconditionally under the default `rules` style, so a COMPLETED table can never end at 3 cells in row 1 with no bottom rule. What is on the slide is one sync's worth of a 23-shape draw — character for character the batch the first sitting watched the pane die in, 'PowerPoint did not respond while drawing shapes 1-10 of 23 (45s)'. Grouping was never REACHED, which is not the same as refused, and the difference is the whole point of this file. What is true: no shape named PowerChart carrying a 'Table, N rows by M columns.' description exists on the slide. Why is unsettled, and the instrument that would settle it is the pane's own status line, which was not read.
secondSitting.hostCondition: Badly degraded, and this is what the sitting mostly measured. Across four probe runs the host stalled reads for 45-60s and left around sixty loose parts — harvey-fill-f0..f22, step-0..3, kpi-box, check-box — from inserts that produced no group. WHETHER THOSE WERE REFUSALS OR TRUNCATED DRAWS IS NOT ESTABLISHED: an earlier version of this entry said 'refused to group 3 of 5 elements at a time', which reads a cause off the same evidence that a draw stopping mid-batch would leave. The probe cannot separate them and neither can a shape list; only the pane's status line can. What IS established and is the point of the sitting: every element that DID group carried its correct description, and not one grouped shape was missing one.
secondSitting.aHostQuirkWorthKnowing: `presentation.setSelectedSlides([newSlideId])` returns without error and `slides.items.length` goes up, but `getSelectedSlides().getItemAt(0)` keeps returning the previously selected slide. Three attempts to give the probe a clean slide all silently read the old one. It changes none of the verdicts — the probe diffs shape ids per run, so what was already there is excluded either way — but a future reader should not believe an added slide is a selected one.
secondSitting.whatTheProbeLearned: It reported `0 of 5 elements carried an altTextDescription`, exit 1, against a build whose descriptions were sitting on that slide as it printed. Three separate confusions, all the same shape: a silent host counted as a wrong answer, a shape read mid-insert counted as a finished one, and an insert that never grouped counted as a description that was never written. Each now has a named cause in the verdict and its own line in the report.

doesNotCover: The table element. It needs one clean insert on a host that answers — and read the PANE'S STATUS LINE when it fails, which is the instrument that says whether the draw finished. Both sittings inferred the blocker from shapes on a slide instead, and the second inferred it wrongly.
PowerPoint on Windows or Mac desktop. This is the web host only.
Whether the description is what a screen reader should ideally say. This checks that the engine's `desc` ARRIVED, not that the copy is good.
n = 1 per element, one slide, one session.
theProbeCostThreeSelfInflictedWounds: It anchored on `tab "Chart"` copied from round.mjs's readiness check. This pane's tabs are Elements/Agenda/Automation, so it reported `no pane on screen` against a pane that was open and healthy.

It passed `--regex` to the CLI's `find`, which takes plain text — the driver applies its regex in JS afterwards, in `refFor`. And it took the FIRST ref in the output rather than the one on the matching line, which `refFor`'s own comment warns lands you in the OneDrive document where `PowerPoint` is undefined.

Worst: its parser could not read the CLI's escaped quotes, so `JSON.parse` threw and every element reported `the host would not list the slide` while the host was answering perfectly. A parser that cannot read the answer reports the same thing as a feature that was never written.
